public_rationale: The causal market claim is supported. Reuters reports substantial incumbent-software declines and identifies the Claude legal plug-in as a catalyst through trader and analyst accounts. Stifel records a 7.8% weekly sector decline and independently describes AI-displacement fears driving selling. Other causes mattered: Reuters also links SAP's earlier fall to weak cloud guidance. This supports a material contribution from AI fears, not sole causation or the assertion that the threat itself is imaginary.
limitations: Causal attribution rests on contemporary market commentary and reporting rather than a controlled event study.
Reuters is used for reported trader explanations because direct records of those conversations were unavailable.
The supported finding excludes the unestablished myth characterization and the exact SAP monthly percentage.

our_interpretation: Assess whether investor fears of AI substitution materially contributed to incumbent software-stock declines, not whether they were the only cause.
Use January 26 through February 26, 2026, following the surrounding reference to the last month.
The word myth is the speaker's characterization. Support for the market mechanism does not establish that the long-term competitive threat is imaginary.
This concerns sector price movements and investor beliefs, not a company's accounting metric; metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous price evidence shows substantial incumbent-software declines, and event timing plus investor or analyst evidence attributes a material part of the selling to fears of AI substitution.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows no substantial relevant decline, or establishes that AI-substitution fears did not materially contribute and that the claimed attribution is mistaken.
